component.text: A newly acquired infection first enters incubation. Its symptoms and mutation effects remain dormant until incubation finishes; most strains also remain non-contagious during this period.

Climate changes that clock. A strain poorly adapted to heat or cold incubates more slowly there while accumulating adaptation pressure. Enough exposure can produce heat adaptation, cold adaptation, and eventually thermal homeostasis.

Infectivity controls exposure probability. Infection strength also decides whether an incoming strain can displace an established infection. Cure resistance modifies treatment difficulty. Lifespan can be finite or unlimited, while self-destruct genes can terminate a strain after a configured environmental trigger.
Incubation duration is also part of the Vaccine Maker correction matrix. Matching this lifecycle channel improves batch quality just like matching symptoms, transmissions and mutations.
